analysis.investment_thesis: Puravankara fails virtually every SMILE criterion — market cap of ₹5,340 Cr is 5x outside my sweet spot, D/E of 2.75 is nearly 5x my red-flag threshold, and the company just posted a ₹183 Cr net loss in FY25 with free cash flow of -₹572 Cr. At 23x forward P/E for a loss-making, over-leveraged real estate developer with only 2.7% revenue CAGR over 9 years, there is no margin of safety whatsoever.
key_strengths: Promoter holding at 75% shows strong skin in the game — well above my 50% threshold
Operating margin of 19.5% suggests decent underlying project economics in Bengaluru's residential market
Long-established brand since 1975 with FII interest at 16.7% provides some institutional validation
key_risks: Debt spiral: borrowings jumped from ₹3,325 Cr (FY24) to ₹4,497 Cr (FY25) while finance costs hit ₹555 Cr — rising at 9.6% CAGR, already exceeding EBITDA of ₹377 Cr
Equity erosion: net worth declined from ₹1,883 Cr to ₹1,619 Cr in one year as company burned ₹183 Cr net loss and OCF collapsed to -₹531 Cr in FY25
No growth story: revenue CAGR of just 2.7% over 9 years with operating income CAGR of -1.7% — this is a stagnant business, not a multibagger candidate
red_flags: Market cap ₹5,340 Cr — 5x above my ₹1,000 Cr upper limit for SMILE
D/E of 2.75 — nearly 5x my 0.6 red-flag threshold; total debt ₹4,332 Cr vs equity ₹1,619 Cr
Loss-making in FY25 (net loss ₹183 Cr) with ROE of -10% — no P/E applicable
FCF swung from +₹842 Cr (FY24) to -₹572 Cr (FY25) in a single year — alarming reversal
EV/EBITDA of 21.3x is absurd for a developer with flat 9-year revenue and rising debt costs
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Puravankara is the antithesis of a SMILE candidate. At ₹5,340 Cr market cap, it sits in mid-cap territory where price discovery is efficient and information asymmetry — my edge — is minimal. The financial picture in FY25 is genuinely alarming: finance costs of ₹555 Cr consumed 148% of EBITDA (₹377 Cr), producing a net loss of ₹183 Cr. Debt has surged 35% in a single year (₹3,325 Cr → ₹4,497 Cr), and equity is being destroyed rather than compounded. This is the classic real estate developer trap — land-heavy balance sheet, project delays, and a cost of debt that outpaces project returns.

The 9-year revenue CAGR of just 2.7% (₹1,584 Cr in 2016 → ₹2,014 Cr in FY25) tells the full story: despite India's enormous real estate cycle tailwind, Puravankara has barely grown in nominal terms. The OCF collapse to -₹531 Cr in FY25 signals either heavy project launches consuming working capital or stalled collections — neither is comforting. Even if I were to hunt in real estate, I would want a small, hungry developer at 8-10x earnings with a clean balance sheet riding the affordable housing wave. Puravankara, at 23x forward P/E with no earnings visibility, negative FCF, and a debt load that would concern a Buffett-style analyst let alone a Kedia, deserves a hard pass.
